_doc: 1.12.0 (improvement slice 3, S3-T5, 2026-08-22) — ONE postflop number, the
new `late_street_bet`: unauthored -> 0.5. At an unopened turn or river the
nit now bets its value hands more, so fewer of its hands check through to a
showdown with no money in the middle. Half its showdown hands arrived that
way, the largest share on the roster, and the calling dial cannot reach them
because they contain no calling decision.
0.5 rather than the 1.0 the field allows, because the response SATURATES
there: over 12,000 hands the two dials are indistinguishable on
went-to-showdown (0.5862 vs 0.5854 against a 0.6144 baseline) and on the
checked-down share, so the deeper dial buys aggression factor and a flatter
per-bucket betting spread without buying any showdown reduction.
Measured at the shipped value: went-to-showdown -2.8 points, hands checked
down to showdown -1.4 points, aggression factor 1.514 -> 1.537 inside its
(0.6, 2.4) band. Sweep and derivation:
docs/ai-dlc/research/slice3-calldown/t5-report.md.
[UNVERIFIED] — no committed source gives a population unopened-late-street
bet frequency for this archetype; the value is fit to the went-to-showdown
gate, and the lever moves leads as well as stabs because the engine cannot
tell them apart.
1.11.0 (improvement slice 3, S3-T2, 2026-08-22) — ONE postflop number,
`call_looseness`: 0.45 -> 0.32. The theory contract's grounded
fold-to-continuation-bet band for this archetype is 60-75 and the nit was
folding 35.9% of the time; the direction is unambiguous and this is the only
lever that speaks to it directly. The dial STOPS AT 0.32 because the alpha
fold-ceiling test, at its pinned seed, admits no lower dial: alpha = f/(1+f)
caps how often a bluff-catcher may fold before a balanced bettor's bluffs
become free money, and at the half-pot bet where that binds the nit is left
with 0.0197 of headroom at 0.32 — about 1.5 binomial standard errors on that
fixture's 1,250 catchers — 0.0021 at 0.31, and a breach at 0.30. That is a
measurement on one fixture at one seed, not a law of the game. So the nit
reaches 43.5% and no further on this lever; the rest of its fold-to-c-bet
gap is not the calling dial's to close, and why is filed as an engine-lever
defect in docs/ai-dlc/ledger/flywheel-slice3-calldown.md — the dial is
hand-strength-blind, so it moves air (already folding ~0.89 at a half-pot
bet) by the same odds factor as the marginal pairs where the gap lives.
`continue_ref` stays FROZEN at 0.6 and `stickiness` at 0.6;
re-syncing either would restore the old raise:call coupling and delete the
N-LOGIT mechanism. Derivation, provenance triples and the pre-registered
went-to-showdown floor:
docs/ai-dlc/research/slice3-calldown/t2-preregistration.md.
1.10.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T2b, 2026-08-17) — the open is authored
per seat and the 3-bet multiplier gains a second rung. Before this change
the pack opened 3.0bb with share 1.000 from all eight opening seats, 109
times per 4,000 hands.
Tighter but bigger is correct poker for this seat and the weights say so:
it takes the small size least often of the three regulars at every seat
(0.10 early, 0.62 late) and carries the most mass on the bigger blind
sizes. A player opening few hands and wanting folds does not shade
downward the way a wide opener does.
The seat ladder and the small-blind bump are the tag's; see its 1.10.0
entry.
This pack has the least room of the six on the determinism guard — its
share of near-unanimous decision contexts runs 0.148 to 0.178 against a
0.20 ceiling. Bet size does not enter that statistic, but any later edit
that changes how often the nit ACTS is measured against those numbers
first.
Every rung is on the 0.5bb grid the rest of the roster uses, and no size or
multiplier here is producible by exactly one pack. A first draft gave this
pack a private off-size rung; measured, one such open named the seat with
certainty, which is the tell the slice exists to remove rather than a way to
differentiate. Personas are separated by WEIGHT — how often each shared size
is taken — and by frequency statistics, never by owning a size.
The bounds are grading rather than taste. A non-blind regular's open stays at
or under 3.0 because `_map_vs_3bet` and `_map_vs_4bet` refuse the whole hand
above `_STD_OPEN_CAP`; both exclude blind openers, which is why the blinds may
go higher. 3-bet rungs stay at or under 3.5, the vs-3-bet cap.
[UNVERIFIED] — the weights. RES-B 4/6.1 sources the LEVELS and confirms the
seat-blind scalars; no committed source gives a distribution of open sizes by
seat at live $2/$3. The ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) carries the measured effect,
the roster-level statement about which direction the levels moved, and why.
THIS PACK DELIBERATELY TAKES NO PART in T5's wet-flop fix, and the reason
is measured rather than stylistic. The three regulars needed a third-pot
bet on wet flops between them, because without one that bet named `station
or fish` outright; the tell is a property of the CLASS, so what the fix has
to move is the class's average weight at that cell, and how that average is
split between the three members is a per-persona question. This pack takes
none of it on two grounds that agree. Poker: a nit taking a cheap stab on a
coordinated board is the least characteristic of the three. Measurement:
sizing is not a pure sizing lever — a pack's size mix scales how often it
bluffs (the F2 joint law) — and an 8% third-pot share here cost this pack
2.8% of its wet-flop bluff mass, which took its share of near-unanimous
decision contexts from 17.6% to 21.1% and failed the determinism guard on
one of five seeds. It is the only pack on the roster without the headroom
to spend; the rest sit between 2.9% and 14.0%. The tag and lag carry the
class's whole share instead, at 14% and 16%.
1.9.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T5, 2026-08-16) — postflop bet sizes are
re-weighted so this seat is no longer identifiable by size alone. The
realised bucket table for the whole roster is in the ticket ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) rather than here — see the
tag's 1.8.0 entry for why.
The flat `sizing` block had no 0.33 at all, so a pack that leads out could
never make a small bet; it has one now. `river_value` gains a medium size
for the same reason as the tag's, and the `raise` block was widened at the
same time and that part was wasted — no bot can reach it.
Every value stays on the grader's recognised grid {0.33, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0,
1.5}; nothing is jittered continuously. No 1.5 is authored here — see the
tag's 1.8.0 entry for why an overbet is the one size this slice does not
hand out.
[UNVERIFIED] — no committed source in this repo gives a population
distribution of bet sizes at low-stakes full ring. See the calling
station's 1.7.0 entry for the one sourced observation this is anchored on.
1.8.0 (de-robotization slice 1, 2026-08-15, review rework) — `vs_rfi`,
`vs_limpers` and `vs_3bet` are answered per seat. Facing a raise, the fold
runs 89.64% in the big blind, 93.30% cutoff/button, 94.96% early and 95.17%
in the small blind, against a flat 94.18% before.
That 5.5-point spread is the roster's narrowest in absolute terms and its
WIDEST in relative terms — the big blind continues 2.14x as often as the
small blind and 1.55x as often as the button. Judging a tight range by
percentage points understates it; a nit adjusting less than a lag is the
archetype, and widening it to match would trade one defect for a worse one.
[UNVERIFIED] — per-seat defence targets have no committed source.
1.6.0 (R9-LOOSEFIT rev4, 2026-08-04) — ONE postflop number, `call_looseness`:
0.6 -> 0.45, so the nit folds materially more at facing nodes than it did
and more often than tag wherever the lever reaches (self leg + population
sweep, see docs/ai-dlc/specs/r9-loosefit-rev4.md). `continue_ref` is
DELIBERATELY NOT moved and stays at 0.6 — it is the frozen calibration
anchor the RAISE merit divides by, so re-syncing it with `call_looseness`
would restore the old coupling and delete that feature. `stickiness` is
also untouched at 0.6.
